events.title: Auditions for BEARS BEARS BEARS BEARS BEARS
events.description:
Attention local actors! Dreamwell Theatre’s next show will be BEARS BEARS BEARS BEARS BEARS by local playwright gwen doctor, directed by Nicole Terry! Auditions will take place 11/6 at 1pm-6pm in ICPL’s Meeting Room E, and 11/8 at 12pm-5pm in ICPL’s Meeting Room D.

A community of bears struggle to navigate in a world that is changing faster than they can understand, as the encroachment of humanity transforms both their home and their relationships. Blending absurd humor with quiet heartbreak, the play explores survival, identity, and what is lost when the natural world collides with the human one.

This show will be a workshop process, involving collaborative conversation with the playwright.

We hope to see you there!

events.title: Glocal at Iowa Me – Iowa – the World
events.description:
IN PARTNERSHIP WITH IOWA CITY PUBLIC LIBRARY, UI INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMS, AND UI INTERNATIONAL EDUCATION MONTH COMMITTEE ​
​​
To celebrate International Education Month, this program features students speaking about their most meaningful “glocal” (where/how the global and the local intersect) experiences while at the University of Iowa.

Using the unique presentation style of Pecha Kucha, meaning “chit-chat” in Japanese, presenters will have six minutes to share 20 timed slides. Their stories and images focus on culture and curiosity from diverse perspectives–and the lessons they’ve learned about life as students in a wide world. A panel discussion with Q&A will follow the presentations.

Nhelia Alemo is a third-year university of Iowa student pursuing a bachelor’s in political science and master’s in public affairs. She is a Congolese American born in Kinshasa and raised in the Midwest. Her global experiences have been grounded on my identity and navigating cultural differences from her upbringing and the outside world. She has taken initiative through policy writing and college extracurriculars to continue expanding her global competency, including being part of the Iowa City Foreign Relations Council intern program.

Ellie Godsoe is a fourth year student from Buffalo, New York, studying English and Creative Writing and Screenwriting with a minor in International Studies. She participated in the Irish Writing Program in Dublin, Ireland, in the summer of 2024. This past summer, she returned to Dublin to complete an internship with Fishamble, an internationally acclaimed Irish theatre company. After graduating, Ellie intends to pursue an MFA in writing to continue interacting and connecting with unique perspectives from across the world.

Sean Keene is a fourth-year student from Columbia, Missouri, majoring in political science, journalism, and Spanish, with a focus on Latin American politics. Sean has participated in four unique programs during his time at Iowa, studying in Spain, Chile, and Paris, and interning in Rome. After graduating, he plans to attend grad school to earn a Ph.D. in political science and international relations. As of this moment Sean has been to 25 countries and wants to try and get to 30 before graduating in May.

Andrés Restrepo-Sánchez is a PhD candidate in Sociocultural Anthropology, whose research explores the connections between reproductive justice, obstetric violence, and birth reform in Medellín, Colombia. He earned a BS in Nursing and an MA in Cultural Studies in Bogotá, Colombia, and then moved to Iowa in 2021 to pursue his PhD with the support of a Fulbright scholarship. Andrés is also a birth doula, tarot reader, crochet and puzzle enthusiast, and RPG and fantasy fan.

Harry Siraj is a first-year law student at the University of Iowa College of Law and a recent University of Iowa graduate, where he studied Political Science and graduated with high distinction and Phi Beta Kappa honors. Originally from Kerala, India, Harry is passionate about exploring the different facets of the legal field as he begins his law school journey. Outside the classroom, his interests include art and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.

events.title: Friday Crafternoons
events.description:
Need a creative break at the end of the week? Swing by the Stanley on Friday afternoons to work on a craft project of your choice.

Bring your own in-progress project or start a new one using the various supplies provided. Try your hand at sketching, coloring, knitting, embroidery, origami, and so much more in a relaxing, low-pressure environment. Stay as long as you like and make new connections. Light snacks will be provided.

Friday Crafternoons occurs almost every Friday at the Stanley Museum of Art lobby and is free and open to all.

events.title: Art & Write Night
events.description:
Join the long, rich, historical tradition of artists creating in our spaces.

Professional, aspiring, and amateur artists alike, make our museum your muse. The return of this popular program series welcomes guests into the Museum of Natural History’s magical gallery spaces after-hours to work on sketching or writing projects with other campus and community artists.

Tell a friend, grab a notebook, and join us on the first Friday of each month. We’ll provide a new inspo prompt for each session and will sometimes move about the Museum but we’ll always start in Bird Hall on the third Floor of Macbride Hall. Join anytime between 6-8 p.m. and feel free to participate in a themed creation challenge or work on your own project with our exhibits as inspiration. We’ll save the last 15-30 minutes of each session to share what we’ve been working on, connecting with others (optional, of course!).

Please note, the Museum is typically closed during this time, meaning the main entrance to Iowa Hall (atop the large staircase outside on the east side of Macbride Hall) will be closed and locked. All other building doors will be open, offering access to the Ground Floor of Macbride Hall, restrooms, stairs and elevator to the third floor galleries where this program takes place. Bird Hall is located on the third floor of Macbride Hall and can be reached by stairs or by taking the elevator to the third floor of the building.

Special thanks to Blick Art Materials for supplying extra art materials. Make sure to check in with us in Bird Hall to check out a variety of special art tools and supplies.

events.title: Iowa City Songwriters Festival – Nathan Graham and Todd Partridge
events.description:
When you think of a singer-songwriter, who comes to mind? Nathan Graham says it probably isn’t somebody who looks like he does. And he wants to change that. Raised in Chicago on Prince and Earth, Wind & Fire, Graham bridges South Side Blues with Nashville Americana to deliver a bittersweet and soulful sound. Starting out backing blues singers at famous haunts like Buddy Guy’s Legends and Kingston Mines, he spent a decade building his career as a guitar-for-hire before forming bands to perform his own music and lyrics.

Todd Partridge has been a fixture on the Midwest music scene for over 25 years, performing a gritty blend of American roots music steeped in blues, folk, country, classic rock, and Americana. Raised among the barns and cornfields of the Midwest prairie, his songwriting carries the raw honesty and weathered soul of Iowa itself. Todd has performed and recorded with bands including Black Light Syndrome, Salamagundi, and the critically acclaimed King of the Tramps, where he spent a decade touring across the U.S. and Europe and released five albums of self-described “Whiskey Gospel” music.

events.title: Jack SPLAT! 2026
events.description:
Send Halloween out with a SPLAT! Don’t toss your Jack-O-Lanterns in the garbage—give them one last hurrah by letting us toss them from up high instead. This free outdoor event is presented by New Pioneer Food Co-op and Urban Acres Realtors (Sean McIntyre, Ben & Whitney Russell, Tundi Brady, Cathy Pugh, and Nicki Thompson).

We’ll be dropping pumpkins from the northwest corner of the parking ramp next to Chauncey Swan Park. Bring your ghoulish gourd, grab a spot with your blanket or lawn chairs, and get ready to watch the pumpkins fly. Come for the SPLATS, but stick around for outdoor activities and a warm breakfast from local food vendors.

Food Vendors: Travelin’ Tom’s Coffee (more coming soon!)

Activity Partners: Coming soon!

How It Works:
Pumpkin drop-off will start at 9:15 a.m. in Chauncey Swan Park on Saturday, November 7th
Activities will begin around 9:30 a.m.
Pumpkin SPLATS will start at 10 am. All pumpkins will be dropped by our team.
Prep Your Pumpkin:
Pumpkins must be gutted (this is Jack SPLAT, not Jack THUD).
Please remove candles, artificial lighting, or any other decorations that are in or attached to the pumpkin. This includes stickers, ribbons, and remnants of candle wax inside.
We compost Jack Splat pumpkins. Ones that have been painted or coated with a preserving sealant should not be added to a compost pile. Pumpkins coated with glitter should not be composted.
We reserve the right to reject your pumpkin if it doesn’t meet our Jack Splat standards.

events.title: Live Your Best Life Sensory Walk & 5K
events.description:
Join us for the Live Your Best Life Sensory Walk & 5K, an inclusive charity run and walk in lowa City designed for participants of all abilities. Whether you’re a seasoned runner chasing a new PR, a casual walker enjoying the morning with friends, or a family looking for a fun community event, this is for you.
Hosted by Systems Unlimited, this event supports people living with disabilities and mental health needs across Eastern lowa. For 55 years, Systems Unlimited has worked to remove barriers and create opportunities so the people we serve can live healthy, active, and fulfilling lives.
Participants can choose between two options:
5K Run/Walk – A scenic course perfect for runners, walkers, and anyone looking to challenge themselves. For this run, you will experience the sensory stations on the 1-Mi route but primarily will have a station free route to focus on your run and enjoy the scenery.
1-Mile Sensory Walk – A relaxed, accessible walk with sensory stations placed throughout the route designed to engage the senses and ensure everyone can experience the pride of reaching the finish line.
The event takes place at the beautiful Terry Trueblood Recreation Area, one of lowa City’s most scenic outdoor spaces. After crossing the finish line, join us at the post-race celebration inside the Terry Trueblood Lodge for music, snacks, community vendors, and fun photo opportunities.
Whether you run, walk, roll, or cheer, you’ll be part of a meaningful event that celebrates inclusion, community, and living your best life.
Register early to guarantee your event shirt and race materials as supplies are first come, first served.

events.title: Flash Forward
events.description:
Flash Forward is PorchLight’s monthly studio session for writers interested in short form writing: flash fiction, micro essays, prose poetry, and more. Join us to learn more about these miniature marvels. Each session includes a discussion of short form works we love, a generative writing prompt, optional sharing, and light positive feedback.

Whether you’re new to these very short forms or an old hand, we’d love to have you join us!

First meeting is free. If you decide you want to become a regular group member purchase a monthly membership for as little as $5 here. Memberships help us keep the Porchlight on!
